children: The Commission rejected the proposition that internal communication or courier delays could determine or alter the commencement of the statutory timeline for filing a written statement. The ruling affirms that a party cannot rely on delays in its internal document-handling mechanisms to seek an extension of the prescribed period for filing its response before the consumer commission.

In Waaree Energies Ltd. v. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. (CC/148/2025), the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has clarified that the period for filing a written statement begins from the date of service of notice at the contractual address of the party, and not from the date on which the notice is received through its internal courier or administrative channels.

The Commission rejected the proposition that internal communication or courier delays could determine or alter the commencement of the statutory timeline for filing a written statement. The ruling affirms that a party cannot rely on delays in its internal document-handling mechanisms to seek an extension of the prescribed period for filing its response before the consumer commission.
For the Complainant: Mr. Saurav Agrawal, Advocate, along with Mr. Himanshu Satija, Ms. Ripul Swati, Mr. Tushar Nair and Mr. Pulkit Khanduja, Advocates.
For the Opposite Party: Mr. Jayant Mehta, Senior Advocate, along with Mr. Anandh Venkataramani, Mr. Saket Satapathy, Mr. Naval Sharma and Ms. Nikita Sharma, Advocates.
